REGULAR EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  APRIL 25, 2022

CALL MEETING TO ORDER
A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order by CHAIR SCHMITZ at 7:02 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall.

SALUTE TO THE FLAG

ROLL CALL
Committee Members Present:  Brtis, Shinn, Silvano, Griggs, Robinson, Schachter,
  Ciarolla, Schmitz, and Martin (joined at 7:05 pm)
Committee Members Absent:  Harik and Nilsen
City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager, Alexa Davis
  Community Services Supervisor, Rosa Pinuelas
  Maintenance Superintendent, Mike Goldsmith
APPROVAL OF MINUTES
MEMBER BRTIS moved seconded by MEMBER SILVANO to:
  APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE MARCH 28, 2022, REGULAR
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES AS PRESENTED.
MEMBER CIAROLLA abstained from the vote.
There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.
AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN /ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA
None.
STAFF ITEMS
A. EQUESTRIAN FEES REVIEW
Supervisor Pinuelas provided a verbal overview per written report.
MEMBER SILVANO asked if costs associated with maintenance have increased and
whether fees should be increased for next year as a result.

MEMBER SHINN recommended increasing fees in small increments as opposed to all
at once. ACM Davis noted that the City’s sports field fees are increased 2% yearly
similar to a cost-of-living adjustment and that staff has seen increases in water usage.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
APRIL 25, 2022
  1
 MEMBER SILVANO noted that fees have not been raised in about six years and that
she recommends looking at increasing trainer fees.

ACM Davis shared that staff is in process of conducting a review of trainer fees,
licensing, and permit requirements with the City Attorney as there is currently no fee for
trail riding operation and that the item would be brought back to the Committee.

MEMBER SILVANO shared that she didn’t think the $1000 per day fee should be raised
but that the other fees should be reviewed.

CHAIR SCHMITZ asked if the equestrian fees could be brought back in May with the
trainer license and permit fee updates and include examples of cost of living
adjustments to be reviewed all at once before going to City Council in June.

ACM Davis affirmed that could be done but noted the trainer licensing and permit
updates includes code updates which might cause a delay but that staff would work to
meet the schedule.

MEMBER SILVANO stated that the Committee should also consider readdressing the
issue of trainers paying for one ring yet restricting usage of the adjacent ring when
running clinics, essentially controlling all the rings but only paying for one.

MEMBER CIAROLLA asked about the Cal Water watering restriction notice and if the
City would also be imposing restrictions noting that horse shows use a lot of water.

ACM DAVIS affirmed that the restrictions have recently been adopted by City Council.

CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that water costs have increased, and violations of water usage
restrictions would result in fees.

MEMBER CIAROLLA asked if fees would be increased to account for spikes in water
usage as a result of water usage during horse shows.

CHAIR SCHMITZ directed staff to consult with the City Attorney regarding that question.

CHAIR SCHMITZ inquired if MEMBER SILVANO wanted the Committee to consider
removing Activity F altogether. MEMBER SILVANO affirmed that they should because
trainers do not just use one ring for their clinics.

MEMBER SHINN stated that if dressage trainers want to restrict usage of the ring
adjacent to the one they are using for safety reasons, they should pay to reserve both
rings which would allow them to do that.

CHAIR SCHMITZ asked for clarification as to if the Committee wanted to require a
trainer to reserve both rings if they wanted to run a clinic.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
APRIL 25, 2022
  2
 MEMBER MARTIN stated trainers would have to be ok with someone using the
adjacent arena at the same time if they chose not to reserve it as it is a public park.

MEMBER SILVANO stated trainers restrict usage of the adjacent ring without reserving
it by saying that usage of the adjacent ring has to stop because they are running a
clinic.

CHAIR SCHMITZ asked if there were issues across the board.

MEMBER SILVANO stated she has often heard complaints although it hasn’t occurred
in some time because there haven’t been many clinics lately.

MEMBER GRIGGS says that some are ok to turn their horses out while a clinic is
occurring and that it just depends on the horse.

CHAIR SCHMITZ suggested including language in the rental agreement that states that
if a trainer will be holding a clinic, they will only have use of the ring they have rented
because the rings around that ring will be open for public use.

MEMBER SHINN suggested adding language stating that there is an option to rent the
second ring for those who have safety concerns.

ACM Davis asked if it still made sense to have two rates for the one ring rental option,
with one rate for usage less than five hours and another for usage over five hours.

MEMBER SILVANO stated that it doesn’t make sense because staff has to prep the
rings beforehand, so the rings are closed for the whole day or from the day before until
the rental is done, regardless of the length of the rental.

MEMBER SHINN recommended making it the same regardless of rental length.

MEMBER GRIGGS stated the ring would need to be closed because people will use it
that morning.

CHAIR SCHMITZ summarized the Committee’s direction to explore what it means to
have a cost of living adjustment to fees and to review the business license updates for
horse trainers and brought back to report at the May meeting while working to have the
code updated.

B. EQUINE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS EFFORTS
ACM DAVIS provided a verbal overview per written report.

MEMBER SHINN thanked and commended staff for their great work and efforts for the
project.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
APRIL 25, 2022
  3
 C. 2022 FIRE MITIGATION SUMMARY

ACM Davis provided a verbal overview per written report.

MEMBER SHINN noted there were no incidents with regards to fireworks last year.

MEMBER GRIGGS noted she still heard fireworks in her neighborhood.

CHAIR SCHMITZ shared that the idea is to strengthen the suppression efforts and that
the canvasing teams have great tactics and are able to suppress the use of fireworks.
She added that the item would be up for a vote the next night’s City Council meeting.

D. EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

There were no questions or comments regarding the log.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E. MAYOR'S RIDE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief update, sharing details of the event’s schedule.

F. CHANDLER PLAYGROUND SURVEY (VERBAL REPORT)

ACM Davis provided a brief update. She noted that the Park and Activities Commission
recommended the concept of a playground to City Council specifically addressing
Equestrian safety for both equestrians and families visiting the park. She also noted the
item would go to the City Council during the second meeting in May.

G. AMBASSADOR PROGRAM UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief update noting further research would be done
before bringing the item to the Committee.

COMMITTEE REPORTS

A. ADOPT-A-TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

Superintendent Goldsmith shared details regarding the Chandler Arena Renovation.

B. MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

None.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
APRIL 25, 2022
  4
 A.  AMBASSADOR PROGRAM

Supervisor Pinuelas noted this item would be brought back at a future meeting.

B.  EQUESTRIAN RECOGNITION

Supervisor Pinuelas shared that the donation goals had not been met this item so this
item would be brought back in May with some alternative ideas and encouraged the
Committee to continue soliciting donations.

C.  CHANDLER ARENA HORSE FACILITY IMPROVEMENTS

None.

MEMBER GRIGGS asked if there would be a big horse show in July. Superintendent
Goldsmith noted Las Amigas used to hold one in July but was no longer doing so.

MEMBER MARTIN shared that the PVPHA board is looking for two new board
members.

CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the Equestrian Committee meeting 7:37 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

__________________________  __________________________
Rosa Pinuelas  Velveth Schmitz, Chair
Community Services Supervisor
